FEEDBACK: [APPLICABILITY] MainShape and CalculationCaseShape nltl:shearForceDirection constraints: The candidate requires every calculation case linked to a ship, and every calculationCase globally targeted by CalculationCaseShape, to have nltl:shearForceDirection nltl:positiveShearForce. The requirement specifies the Cf schedule only for positive shear force; non-positive cases are not made invalid by this requirement. Required change: Apply the Cf schedule and associated calculation validation conditionally to calculation cases whose direction is nltl:positiveShearForce, without making positiveShearForce mandatory for every linked or globally targeted calculation case.

[APPLICABILITY] I2-051-ShipShape > nltl:hasCalculationCase > nltl:shearForceDirection: The candidate does not constrain calculation cases to the required nltl:positiveShearForce value. Its SPARQL condition merely selects positive-shear cases, so a ship containing only a non-positive or otherwise uncontrolled direction can bypass the entire Cf distribution and FI calculation requirement. Required change: Add sh:hasValue nltl:positiveShearForce to the shearForceDirection property constraint, or otherwise make positive-shear applicability mandatory for every case to which this requirement is applied.

[LOGIC] I2-051-ShipShape / nltl:hasCalculationCase / nltl:shearForceDirection: The nested calculation-case constraint requires every calculation case linked to a ship to have nltl:shearForceDirection equal to nltl:positiveShearForce. This prevents other shear-force directions from being represented, contrary to the stated applicability that the Cf and FI checks apply only to positive-shear cases. Required change: Remove the unconditional sh:hasValue nltl:positiveShearForce restriction from the linked calculation-case node constraint; retain positive-shear applicability in the conditional calculation check. | [FORMULA] I2-051-ShipShape / sh:sparql: The SPARQL check accepts a reported shear force that differs from Cf × FIB by an invented relative/absolute tolerance, although the requirement states the equality FI = Cf × FIB and supplies no tolerance. Required change: Enforce the stated formula equality directly, or use a tolerance only if an authoritative requirement explicitly specifies one.

[LOGIC] I2-051-ShipShape/sh:sparql: The SPARQL constraint rejects every positive-shear case whose position lies between 0.6 LUI and 0.9 LUI unless Cf is exactly 0 or 1, although the requirement specifies Cf only for the aft-through-0.6 LUI interval and the 0.9-LUI-through-forward interval and imposes no Cf value in the intervening interval. Required change: Do not produce a violation solely because a positive-shear position is in the unspecified 0.6-to-0.9 LUI interval; enforce the Cf boundary values only within their explicitly specified intervals, while retaining FI = Cf × FIB for positive-shear cases. | [CONTROLLED_VOCABULARY] I2-051-ShipShape/nltl:hasCalculationCase/[nltl:shearForceDirection]: The direction value is constrained only by cardinality, so an arbitrary resource or literal can be supplied; the SPARQL formula is then skipped unless the value happens to equal nltl:positiveShearForce, allowing an invalid direction value to bypass the positive-shear applicability condition. Required change: Constrain nltl:shearForceDirection values to the canonical shearForceDirectionValue class, while retaining the conditional formula enforcement only for nltl:positiveShearForce.
